question: Does the law clearly demarcate the functions/responsibilities of the parastatal vis-à-vis the ULG?
step2_answer: ANSWER: No. The law does not clearly demarcate BWSSB's functions from the ULG's. Water supply is assigned in full to the City Corporation (Scenario B), and BWSSB's Act gives BWSSB the same function across the whole metropolitan area with no carve-out. Proposed score 0. | EVIDENCE: (1) ULG side, Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024 (Act 36 of 2025), s.111(1) and Schedule I, Core Functions item (v): 'Water supply for domestic, industrial and commercial purposes'. Item (vi) also lists 'Public health, sanitation including storm water drains, conservancy and solid and liquid waste management'. Section 111(1) makes it the City Corporation's duty 'to render necessary services to the inhabitants ... in respect of the matters enumerated as core functions in the First Schedule'. Section 197(1)(b) vests 'All sewers, drains, drainage works...' in the City Corporation. Ward Committee functions in the Act include ensuring 'water supply maintenance in the ward' and 'sewerage system maintenance in the ward'. (2) Parastatal side, BWSSB Act 1964 s.15(1): the Board 'shall be charged with the general duty of providing a supply and improving the existing supply of water in the Bangalore Metropolitan Area and of making adequate provision for the sewerage and the disposal of the sewage'. Section 15(2)-(3) covers wholesome water for domestic purposes 'to every part of the Bangalore Metropolitan Area'. This is not limited by aspect (bulk versus distribution), area or scale. question: Is the parastatal's territorial/geographic jurisdiction specifically defined in it's enabling law?

The Board's duties are tied to this area: s.26 (vesting of works for supplying water to the Bangalore Metropolitan Area), s.27(1) (water works for supplying the Bangalore Metropolitan Area) and s.15(2)(a).
